result: In a German university post-COVID clinic registry (n=1022; 411 with two visits), 31.3% met ME/CFS criteria at median 255 days post infection and 19.4% at median 402 days; self-reported fatigue fell from 83.7% to 72.7%.
reason: Uncontrolled clinic cohort gives a proportion among referred long COVID patients (like Dehlia), not incidence vs uninfected, so not a replication of the RECOVER HR

result: Among post-COVID clinic patients, 31.3% met ME/CFS criteria at a median 255 days and 19.4% still did at a median 402 days, while self-reported symptoms declined but structured screening scores did not change significantly.
reason: Adds time course in a larger clinic cohort with partial decline in ME/CFS proportion; not the same measure as Charite severity persistence, so extends rather than replicates

result: Multicenter PCR and high-throughput sequencing of blood, feces and saliva found no consistent virus differences between ME/CFS and controls except a lower prevalence of anelloviruses in cases.
reason: Independent multicenter unbiased virome study, same null direction; lower anellovirus prevalence also argues against the TTMV subgroup signal

result: Systematic review of 21 urinary biomarker studies; meta-analysis of 7 urinary free cortisol studies found a significant ME/CFS vs control difference with substantial heterogeneity (direction not stated in abstract).
reason: Meta-analysis of overlapping studies, not an independent cohort; abstract does not state direction and stresses heterogeneity, so it adds caveats rather than replicating

result: SELENOP autoantibodies were found in 9.6-15.6% of 167 CFS patients vs 0.9-2.0% of 545 controls, and positive patients had particularly low deiodinase activity (SPINA-GD), free T3, TT3/TT4 and FT3/FT4 ratios and lower urinary iodine (43.2 vs 58.9 vs 89.0 ug/L).
reason: Same thyroid measures in the previously characterized Dutch subgroup, adding a candidate autoantibody mechanism for low T3 deiodination

result: In 33 PASC, 33 POTS and 33 healthy controls, PASC and POTS both had significantly reduced respiratory sinus arrhythmia on beat-to-beat autonomic testing, with high autonomic symptom burden and poor quality of life in PASC.
reason: Independent long COVID cohort with objective cardiovascular autonomic testing showing abnormalities, same direction; abstract results are truncated

result: In 33 PASC, 33 POTS and 33 controls, PASC showed reduced respiratory sinus arrhythmia and high autonomic symptom burden; no POTS prevalence figure is given in the abstract.
reason: Finding is POTS prevalence in ME/CFS; this is a small long COVID study with no prevalence number in the abstract, already covered by the neuro-lc-autonomic-objective link

result: In 256 participants (34 PASC, ME/CFS by duration, 82 controls), cognitive efficiency fell after orthostatic challenge in disease groups, narrow pulse pressure (<25% of systolic) appeared at 4-5 min, and narrow pulse pressure was associated with slowed information processing in PASC (-1.5, p=0.04).
reason: No cerebral blood flow measured; the narrow pulse pressure during a 10-min orthostatic challenge in recent-onset patients matches the NASA lean finding

result: Disease cohorts had lower cognitive efficiency immediately after an orthostatic challenge than controls, remaining low at 2 and 7 days in >10-year ME/CFS, with hemodynamic changes mediating slower reaction time in PASC.
reason: Same measure (processing speed and reaction time worsening with upright posture), adds mediation by hemodynamics, PASC and illness-duration subgroups

result: Meta-analysis of 7 studies (403 ME/CFS patients) found significantly lower serum acylcarnitine levels than in healthy controls, with high heterogeneity.
reason: Same measure and direction pooled across cohorts; partly overlapping studies and high heterogeneity limit independence
